result.text: Statistically significant treatment benefit over placebo for the primary endpoint of mortality when tecovirimat was dosed at 3, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for 14 days starting Day 4; 10 mg/kg/day selected as the fully effective dose

citations.quote: A statistically significant treatment benefit over placebo for the primary endpoint of mortality was demonstrated when tecovirimat was dosed at 3, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day for 14 days starting at Day 4 after virus inoculation (Appendix 1). 10 mg/kg/day was selected as the fully effective dose to ensure that drug levels used to determine the effective human dose would exceed the minimally effective dose in this model.

target_moa.text: Tecovirimat is an inhibitor of the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope wrapping protein; it targets and inhibits VP37 and blocks its interaction with cellular Rab9 GTPase and TIP47, preventing formation of egress-competent enveloped virions needed for cell-to-cell and long-range dissemination of virus

citations.quote: TPOXX (tecovirimat) is an inhibitor of the orthopoxvirus VP37 envelope wrapping protein.

Tecovirimat targets and inhibits the activity of the orthopoxvirus VP37 protein (encoded by and highly conserved in all members of the orthopoxvirus genus) and blocks its interaction with cellular Rab9 GTPase and TIP47, which prevents the formation of egress-competent enveloped virions necessary for cell-to-cell and long-range dissemination of virus.

modality.text: Small molecule (oral antiviral; immediate release capsules containing tecovirimat monohydrate equivalent to 200 mg of tecovirimat)

key_safety.text: Favorable safety profile; common adverse reactions (>2%) in Study 246-008 (tecovirimat N=359 vs placebo N=90): headache 44 (12%) vs 7 (8%), nausea 16 (5%) vs 4 (4%), abdominal pain 7 (2%) vs 1 (1%), vomiting 7 (2%) vs 0 (0%), diarrhea 7 (2%) vs 2 (2%); one death (pulmonary embolism), the only SAE, not judged related to tecovirimat

There was only one death in Study 246-008; this event was also the only SAE in the trial. The death was due to pulmonary embolism and occurred in a 46-year-old female with a history of lower extremity deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and concomitant use of Depo-Provera.

summary.text: Tecovirimat was developed under the Animal Rule (21 CFR part 314, subpart I) because clinical efficacy trials for smallpox are not feasible and human challenge studies are unethical; it received Fast Track designation in 2005, Orphan Drug designation in 2006, and Rolling Review in 2017. Effectiveness was established on the primary endpoint of mortality in NHP/monkeypox and rabbit/rabbitpox surrogate models, and the Antimicrobial/Antiviral Drugs Advisory Committee voted unanimously (17-0) for approval; the sponsor was granted a material threat medical countermeasure priority review voucher.
